title: Universal halting exceeds every time bound
statement: For every effective machine code scheme $c$ and every function $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the unary language consisting of all-one words of length $n$ such that the most-significant-first binary expansion of $n$ is $1$ followed by a string $s$ for which some advice string $\alpha$ and input $x$ satisfy $s=\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ and the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ with some output is not decidable by any finite-state binary Turing machine within time $C T(n)$ for any constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine code scheme
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine representation scheme, and let
$T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be any function. The unary language of numbers whose
binary expansions begin with $1s$, where $s$ encodes an advice string and an input on
which the machine decoded from that advice halts, is not decidable by a finite binary
Turing machine in time bounded by any constant multiple of $T$.
